q: 1. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Lime stone (calcareous material) supplies the required lime (CaO) content, which forms the major ingredient of cement, hence it is the commonly used raw material.

q: 2. To obtain cement dry powder, lime stones and shales or their slurry, is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix is burnt at 1400°C–1500°C, the clinkering temperature, at which the raw materials fuse to form cement clinker.

q: 3. The chemical ingredient of cement which provides quick setting property to the cement is
explain: Alumina in cement lowers the clinkering temperature and imparts quick setting properties, though excess alumina can weaken the cement.

q: 4. Lime when added in excess quantity
options: caused the cement to expand and disintegrate
lowers the clinkering temperature of cement
explain: Excess free lime in cement remains uncombined, and upon hydration it expands, causing the cement to become unsound and disintegrate.

q: 5. Setting time of cement decreases by adding
explain: Calcium chloride acts as an accelerator, speeding up the hydration reaction and thereby decreasing the setting time of cement.

q: 6. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that, on average, the aggregate particles are coarser, since FM is the sum of cumulative percentages retained on standard sieves divided by 100.

q: 7. The C4AF in cement has the cementing value
explain: Tetracalcium aluminoferrite (C4AF) contributes little to strength and has a poor cementing value compared to the silicate compounds.

q: 8. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1: 3 cement mortar cube) after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS specifications, a 1:3 cement-sand mortar cube of ordinary Portland cement must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 17.5 N/mm² after 7 days.

q: 9. IS sieve no 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: The 10 mm and 4.75 mm sieves fall at the boundary between coarse and fine aggregate classification and are used in grading both types.

q: 10. The aggregate is said to be flaky when
options: its least dimension is three-fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to 1.8 times its mean dimension
explain: An aggregate particle is classified as flaky when its least (thickness) dimension is less than three-fifths (3/5) of its mean dimension.

q: 11. The apparent specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural process in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Apparent specific gravity is the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its absolute (solid) volume, excluding the natural pores within the particles.

q: 12. A moist aggregate is one
options: whose all the pores are filled with water and also having its surface wet
whose all the pores are filled with water but having its surface dry
which do not contain any moisture in the pores but having dry surface
which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface
explain: A moist aggregate has all its pores filled with water and additionally carries free water on its surface, making the surface wet.

q: 13. An aggregate which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface is known as
explain: A 'dry' aggregate condition refers to particles that may retain some internal pore moisture but present a dry outer surface, distinct from the fully saturated-surface-dry or very dry states.

q: 14. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, high alumina cement has
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial setting time and final setting time
lower initial setting time and final setting time
explain: High alumina cement is characterized by a longer initial setting time but a comparatively shorter final setting time than OPC, giving rapid strength gain once setting begins.

q: 15. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: sand stones may be defined into calcareous, siliceous and ferruginous sand stones
concrete using sand stones, cracks due to excessive shrinkage
very hard and close grained crystallized lime stones are suitable aggregates but provide low strength
broken bricks produce a concrete having good fire resisting qualities
explain: All the statements regarding sand stone types, shrinkage cracking, limestone strength, and broken brick fire resistance are correct.

q: 16. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: bulking of sand is caused due to formation of a thin film of surface moisture
fine sand bulks more than coarse sand
with 10% moisture content by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by 50%
the volume of fully saturated sand, is equal to the volume of dry and loose sand
explain: All statements regarding causes of bulking, fine sand bulking more, the 10% moisture bulking figure, and saturated sand volume equaling dry sand volume are correct.

q: 17. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete, is known
explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of solids.

q: 18. The fineness modulus of an aggregate is roughly proportional to
options: average size of the particles in the aggregate
explain: Fineness modulus is an empirical index that correlates roughly with the average particle size of the aggregate — a higher FM indicates coarser average particle size.

q: 19. A concrete using an air entrained cement
options: Is free from segregation and bleeding
explain: Air-entrainment introduces microscopic air bubbles that act like tiny ball bearings within the mix, improving plasticity and workability of the fresh concrete (though it does reduce strength and improve frost resistance too, per this text the key answer selected is improved plasticity/workability).

q: 20. The dimensions of a 35 liter forma for measuring aggregates by volume, are:
explain: A standard 'farma' (gauge box) with dimensions of 27cm × 27cm × 48cm gives a volume of about 35 liters, used for volumetric batching of aggregates on site.

q: 21. Hydration of cement is due to the chemical action of water with
explain: Cement hydration involves the chemical reaction of water with all the major clinker compounds, including dicalcium silicate, tricalcium silicate, and tricalcium aluminate.

q: 22. Adding a thin layer of cement mortar to the surface of concrete is known as
explain: Rendering (rendeting) refers to applying a thin coat/layer of cement mortar over a concrete or masonry surface, typically for finishing or protective purposes.

q: 23. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately
explain: As given in this text, the void content within a mass of cement particles (loose powder) is approximately 25%.

q: 24. Low percentage of tricalcium silicate and high percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: Cement low in C3S and high in C2S hydrates slowly with low heat generation and low early strength (though good ultimate strength) — so none of the listed rapid/early/high-heat effects apply.

q: 25. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement gains strength more slowly in the early months due to reduced C3S/C3A content, but eventually catches up to match the strength of ordinary cement.

q: 26. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sans and coarse aggregates
explain: The chemical hydration reaction between cement and water forms the cementitious gel that binds the aggregates together, which is the fundamental source of concrete's strength.

q: 27. If the depth of moist sand in a cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of the sand with fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the moist sand, is
explain: Bulking % = [(h1 - h2)/h2] x 100 = [(15-12)/12] x 100 = 25%, where h1 is the moist sand depth and h2 is the fully inundated (saturated) depth.

q: 28. If X, Y, Z are the fineness moduli of coarse, fine and combined aggregates, the percentage (P) of fine aggregate to combined aggregates, is
explain: The formula for the percentage of fine aggregate needed to achieve a combined fineness modulus, based on the fineness moduli of coarse (X), fine (Y), and combined (Z) aggregates, is p = [(X-Z)/(Z-Y)] x 100.

q: 29. The heat of hydration of cement can be reduced by
options: Reducing proportions of C3A and C3S
Increasing the proportions of C3A and C3S
explain: Since C3A and C3S are the compounds that generate the most heat during hydration, reducing their proportions in the cement composition lowers the overall heat of hydration.

q: 30. For ordinary cement, the maximum expansion by Le Chatelier method should not be more than
explain: As per IS specifications, the maximum permissible expansion for ordinary Portland cement measured by the Le-Chatelier method should not exceed 10mm.

q: 31. For 1 bag of cement (50kg) the quantity of water required is
explain: Using a typical water-cement ratio of about 0.7, the quantity of water required for one 50kg bag of cement works out to approximately 35kg.

q: 32. The degree of grinding of cement is called
explain: Fineness of cement refers directly to the degree to which the clinker has been ground into fine powder.

q: 33. Too much fineness of cement
explain: Very fine cement hydrates faster, generating more heat of hydration, which can lead to thermal cracking in concrete — so both effects (a and b) occur.

q: 34. Light-weight concrete is prepared by
options: using coke breeze, cinder or slag as aggregate in the concrete
explain: Light-weight concrete is commonly prepared using lightweight aggregates such as coke breeze, cinder, or slag, which reduce the overall density of the concrete.

q: 35. Percentage of pozzolanic material containing clay upto 80% used for the manufacture of pozzolana cement is
explain: As given in this text, pozzolanic material (containing up to 80% clay) is blended at about 30% by mass in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 36. The type of cement preferred in the construction of massive concrete dam is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction because it minimizes the heat of hydration, reducing the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 37. The process by which fresh cement concrete is wetted by rain water is known as
explain: Wetting of fresh concrete by rain water is not a controlled/intended process and is not technically classified as curing, wetting (in the technical sense), or raining, so 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 38. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of a cement warehouse, is
explain: A cement warehouse floor carries heavy stacked loads, so codes specify a relatively thick slab, with 25 cm being the maximum recommended thickness for such floors.

q: 39. Find the gel space ratio of concrete with following data: cement = 50 kg, Weight of water = 20 kg
explain: Substituting the given cement and water quantities into the standard gel-space ratio formula (relating the volume of hydration products to total space occupied) gives a ratio of approximately 0.91.

q: 40. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction, as it minimizes the heat of hydration and reduces the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 41. If sea water is used for preparing concrete mix, it
explain: Sea water contains salts that reduce concrete strength, promote corrosion of embedded steel reinforcement, and cause efflorescence — all of these harmful effects occur.

q: 42. A concrete in which dry coarse aggregate are first packed to have the least voids and then the cement sand mortar is injected under pressure to fill all the voids, resulting in a very dense concrete, is known as
explain: This describes pre-packed concrete, where coarse aggregate is placed first and mortar is then grouted under pressure into the voids to produce a dense mass.

q: 43. The cement sand ratio in the ferrocement matrix should not be leaner than
explain: To achieve adequate strength and to properly encase the closely spaced wire mesh, the ferrocement matrix cement-sand ratio should not be leaner than 1:2.5.

q: 44. Pozzolana is essentially a silicious material containing clay upto
explain: As defined in this text, pozzolana is a siliceous material that may contain clay content up to as much as 80%.

q: 45. Humidity causes ……… of cement in bag .
explain: Moisture in humid air can react with cement stored in bags, initiating premature hydration/setting reactions that spoil the cement before use.

q: 46. Modulus of rupture of concrete is measure of :
explain: Modulus of rupture is obtained from a beam flexure test and represents the flexural (bending) tensile strength of concrete.

q: 47. Soundness of the material means the resistance of the material against the effect of :
explain: Soundness specifically refers to a material's ability to resist volume changes/deterioration from repeated cycles of freezing and thawing.

q: 48. *The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as :
explain: Abrasion resistance specifically measures an aggregate's ability to withstand surface wearing action, distinct from crushing or impact resistance.

q: 49. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolana, is :
explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures set relatively slowly, with a specified minimum initial setting time of 120 minutes as per standard requirements.
